$comment: The device transport binding's vectors (DEC-0056, devices.md#transport): HTTP message signatures (RFC 9421 subset) with Content-Digest (RFC 9530). Each case is a FAC-SEM-077 rule input without `answer`: merge the top-level publicBaseUrl, certificates and at into it; `seen` is the receiver's nonce store before the request; `clientCertificateSerial`, when present, is the serial of a mutual-TLS session's client certificate (DEC-0056 item 1); `expect` is accepted or the 401 code, or `organization-closed` (410, DEC-0103) for a closed organization's certificate, whose cases also carry `expectStatus` 410 and `expectClosedAt`. Every case carries one fault (`fault`); the `organization` cases' certificate is also revoked on purpose, to pin step 4 before step 5 (DEC-0103). Keys are fresh, generated for these vectors; only their public halves are here, and ECDSA signatures are not reproducible, so a signer port is tested by verifying its own output. `rfc9421` and `rfc9530` are the RFCs' own examples, run by test/http-signature.test.ts.

rfc9421.section: RFC 9421 Appendix B.2.6, the key test-key-ed25519 (Appendix B.1.4), public half only

cases.note: No private key made this: R = B, S = 1 and k = SHA-512(R ‖ A ‖ base) mod L ≡ 0 (mod 4) under the all-zero key A of order 4, so the cofactorless equation [S]B = R + [k]A holds. Node 20 and 22 accept such a forgery and Node 24 and 26 refuse it (DEC-0045); the binding refuses the key before verifying.
